Title: Register Pose/Motion
Content: New in 2024.2 You can easily register the pose or motion from an FBX file as a file compatible with CLO avatars. Click the Main Menu Avatar Register Pose/Motion menu. Select the type to register, either Pose or Motion. Open the FBX file by clicking on the Open button. Select the Gender of the compatible CLO avatar and select the Shoe Type for female. Note: If the FBX file's joint names do not match the CLO avatar's, it can only be saved and cannot be registered as the CLO-compatible file. For motion, switch to Animation mode to play loaded motion as needed. Click the Save button to save as the Pose(POS) or Motion(MTN) file.

Title: Adjust Avatar Joints
Content: List of Contents Show Avatar Joints FK (Forward Kinematics) IK (Inverse Kinematics) Set Joint Size Change the avatar pose by moving and rotating the avatar joint Show Avatar Joints Hover over the Avatar Display in the 3D window, then click the Show Avatar Joints. FK (Forward Kinematics) You can adjust each joint individually to fine-tune the pose. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and rotation by clicking on the joint. IK (Inverse Kinematics) You can adjust the specific joint, and the organically linked joints are automatically calculated to easily express realistic pose. Change the mode to IK in Avatar Joint window. Set the options as needed. Option Description Full Body When a single joint is modified, it affects all other joints which are organically linked to the single joint. Body Part When a single joint is modified, only directly connected joints are modified. Constrain Joint Translation Activate the option to prevent unwanted movement of the selected joint caused by other moving joints. However, for natural modification of the Avatar, the constrained joint may move slightly. Constrain Joint Rotation Activate the option to prevent unwanted movement of the selected joint caused by other rotating joints. However, for natural modification of the Avatar, the constrained joint may rotate slightly. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and rotation by clicking on the joint. * If the joints and axes of the avatar are symmetrical, you can adjust the joints symmetrically by clicking the symmetric button next to the Gizmo. Note: Human IK created in other 3D software is not compatible with CLO. To import avatars created in other 3D software, the avatar must have the same bone structure and names. To refer to CLO avatars' bone structures and names, please download the files below. Set Joint Size Set the joint size smaller to make selection easier on avatars with a lot of joints. Enter the size in the Avatar Joint window.

Title: Offset Avatar Joint
Content: New in 2024.2 Adjust avatar joint offsets for various body shapes using just a single motion file Note: This can be helpful when the same avatar has varying body shapes. For example, the offset can be adjusted to correct the distance between the hands and hips in a motion when it does not align due to the avatar's body shape. Open the Motion file in Animation Mode. Right-click on the animation layer corresponding to the motion file, and click the Offset Joint menu. Click on the Joint. Rotate directly with the gizmo or adjust each axis in the Offset Joint window. The joint offset is applied to the motion where you right-clicked.

Title: New Library (Beta)
Content: New in 2024.2 List of Contents Switch to New Library Explore Assets Custom Library CLO-SET Easily find and manage assets with an intuitive library window interface! The New Library is being piloted as a beta service first, and will be made generally available at a later date based on your valuable feedback. What do I get with New Library? Freely access and float the New Library whenever needed to use the 3D and 2D windows with more space at other times. Easily explore and utilize various assets. CLO interacts more intuitively with both CONNECT and CLO-SET to seamlessly access content. Create a custom library to build and manage your own assets. Switch to New Library Switch to the New Library by clicking the on the bottom of the existing Library window. The New Library can be freely accessed using the Button on the top right of CLO. Drag the Library window to move or press the ESC key to quickly close it. Note: You can easily revert to the current Library if needed by clicking the Revert to Previous Library button. Explore Assets Assets are categorized into five groups: Garment, Avatar, Fabric, Trim, and Scene. Each category offers default assets by CLO and community assets by CONNECT. Click the category to explore assets. Double-click an asset or drag and drop it into CLO to open it immediately. Community assets are available for free items only, and used items can be found in the tab. Click the Show Preview button to preview the file on a larger thumbnail. Custom Library Create a custom library to build and manage your own assets. Click the Create New Library button on the top. Click the to add folders from your desktop. CLO-SET Link your CLO-SET account to easily access contents! Click the CLO-SET tab. Click the to link your CLO-SET account. Access CLO-SET contents, and double-click an item to open it. Note: You can change, switch or delete linked CLO-SET account by clicking the Profile button. Go back to List of Contents

Title: Open MetaHuman Body Types
Content: Objective Select a desired MetaHuman body type and create an outfit for your MetaHuman in CLO before bringing the outfit to Unreal Engine as USD files. Location Library Click Avatar Folder MetaHuman Double click to download a desired MetaHuman body types Note: Arms need to be bent on export in order for Unreal Engine's USD import pipeline to work properly. Once garments are ready to be exported, apply a pose named 'Default_Pose' in Pose folder to a desired MetaHuman body. A pose named 'Apose' is provided in order for garments to be fit on a desired MetaHuman body with ease, especially around arms. In Marvelous Designer versions below 2024.0.173, applying the two aforementioned poses to a MetaHuman body will result in the error message "No matching avatar" and will not be applied.

Title: 3D State
Content: Record 3D state to compare or check your design process. Open the History window on the left side of CLO. Click the Add 3D State button to record 3D state as a project file. Preview the 3D state by hovering over the 3D state before opening it. Double click the 3D state to open. Right-click on the 3D state to rename, delete or add. Note: When you save a project file(ZPRJ), the 3D State file is also saved with it. The more 3D files that are saved, the bigger the file is. It may slow down the speed when you open and save the file.

Title: Edit Sewing
Content: List of Contents Edit Sewing Select Sewing Move Sewing Adjust Sewing Length Sewing Line Pop-Up Menu Edit Sewing - Select and edit Sewing Lines in the 2D window. - Select the Edit Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Sewing Edit Sewing. Select Sewing - With the Edit Sewing tool selected, click on the Sewing Line to be selected. - The sewing Line will be bolded. - When there are multiple Sewing Lines on the selected Pattern outline, pop-up menu showing all Sewing Line options will appear. - Use the color chip in front of the Sewing Line name to choose the desired one. - The Sewing Lines are ordered in an ascending order, arranging the latest to last. Move Sewing - Select and drag the center of the Sewing Line. - When the selected Sewing Line is on a symmetric Pattern, the second half of the Sewing Line on its symmetric pair will be moved simultaneously. Adjust Sewing Length Adjust Freely - Select and drag one end point of the Sewing Line towards the desired direction. - Only the selected half of the Sewing Line will be adjusted. To match the sewing length of the second half of the Sewing Line, repeat the same process as above. When adjusting the second half of the Sewing Line, a blue point will appear guiding the length of the first half of the Sewing Line. Adjust with Designated Value - Select and drag one end point of the Sewing Line towards the desired direction. - While holding down the mouse, right-click to access the Moving Distance window. - Enter the desired distance the point will be moved. Sewing Line Pop-Up Menu Access Right Click Pop-Up Menu - Right-click on the Sewing Line to be edited to access the pop-up menu. Select All with Same Property - Use this option to select all Sewing Lines with the same property. Fold Strength - Select all Sewing Lines with the same Fold Strength value. Fold Angle - Select all Sewing Lines with the same Fold Angle value. Reverse Sewing - Reverse the direction notch of the selected Sewing Line. Delete Sewing - Delete the selected Sewing Line. - Right-click on the Sewing Line and select Delete Sewing. - When deleting a Sewing Line, its pair will be deleted as well. - Use this option when directional notches are twisted. Merge - Merge Patterns based on the selected Sewing Line. Add Point to Pattern on Start/ Add Point to Pattern on End - Add points to the Pattern outline based on the start or the end point of the Sewing Line. - The point near the directional notch is the start point and the point far from the directional notch is the end point. Deactivate Sewing (Selected) - Deactivate Sewing Lines to disable their functions. - When the selected Sewing Line is deactivated, it will turn white. - When the Simulation is activated, the Patterns with the deactivated Sewing Line will no longer sewn to each other. - To activate the Sewing Line again, right click on the Sewing Line and select Activate Sewing. Hide Sewing - Hide Sewing Lines in the 2D window. - When the Sewing Lines are hidden, they will no longer appear in the 2D window. - To show them again, right click on the Sewing Line and select Show Sewing (All).

Title: Fabric Color
Content: Objective Set the color of the fabric. Location Object Browser Fabric Tab Fabric Item Color Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: A color window appears. Refer to the table below to set the color. Custom Palette ① Edit Color Click the color you want to use from the color field or enter color values. ② Eyedropper Select the color you want to use from the image, inside of the program, or the other websites. ③ Add Color Add the selected color in Custom Palette. ④ Swatch Size Adjust the size of swatches. ⑤ Open/ Save File Open or Save color palette file. ⑥ Reset Reset your Custom Palette. ⑦ Change the view Choose List, Detail, or Icon view to change the view. ⑧ Edit Color Swatch Rename Double-click the swatch to change the name. Reorder Click &amp drag and drop the swatch to change the order. Delete Click the swatch and delete it pressing Delete in keyboard. Palette Library The latest Color Library is provided with Pantone API. ⑨ Add Palette File Import Palette files(ACO, ASO, CCO). Note: You can only save the Pantone colors in CCO format supported by CLO. ⑩ Search Color Search the similar color with the name of the color or the selected color. ⑪ Add Color to Custom Palette Add the color of Palette Library to the Custom Palette. Title: [View Control] Zoom In/Out, Rotation
Content: Objective In CLO, the mouse wheel and the right button can be used to zoom in, zoom out, and rotate the screen. The Maya and 3Ds Max view control methods are also supported alongside the default view control method and interface can be modified as needed and use differently. Operation Move Hold down the mouse wheel and drag to move the screen. If you are using Mac's Magic Mouse, please hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and click-and-drag the left mouse key. Zoom In/Out Scroll down (zoom in) and up (zoom out) the mouse wheel to zoom in and zoom out the screen. Or, hold down Alt Key on the keyboard and the left button of the mouse simultaneously and drag up (zoom out) or down (zoom in). Note: Zoom in or zoom out using the + (zoom in) and - (zoom out) keys on the keyboard (ver2.4.0.) Rotate Hold down the right button of the mouse and drag to rotate the 3D window.

Title: How can I export FBX from CLO to APEXFiz?
Content: [Extract Patterns] is a function that is only supported by the 3D OPTION of APEXFIz. Below is a menu of CLO software. Select necessary avatar and patterns. Select multiple object, not single object. Export without combining vertex Select [Thin] for thickness. Select default [mm] for scale. If textures are required, select embed media. If textures are required, enter a file name and a folder name with half-width characters. Create a unified UV map. At this time, all pattern UVs should be arranged within the 0-1 space in the UV editor, ensuring there is no overlap. Place the pattern UVs according to the knitting direction in APEXFiz, as this direction cannot be changed in the Extract Pattern menu. Textures with alpha(hair, eyelash, etc.) may not be imported correctly. Internal lines(design lines) cannot be imported. Stitch data will not be readable in APEXFiz.

Title: Register Custom OBJ as Buttons
Content: List of Contents Register Button Add Button Register Button - Register custom OBJ files as buttons as needed. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select Materials Button Register Button. - Or, select a desired button style from the Object Browser Button Tab. Then, navigate to the Property Editor to find the Register Button button next to the Shape toggle down menu. Add Button - Follow the indicated path above and select the Register Button button. - The Register Button window appears. - Name the button. - Select the Search button next to the OBJ menu to choose a custom OBJ file. - Select the + button next to the Thumbnail menu to load a custom image to be the buttons thumbnail. - Select OK to complete the registration. - The registered button appears in the following path: Object Browser Button Tab Button (Select a Style) Property Editor Shape. - The registered button is saved into the CLO library under Hardware and Trims Button &amp Buttonhole Button.

Title: Why do I have to pay tax?
Content: Please note that if you have a correct registered VAT ID, you can add VAT ID on Billing Address and your tax will be waived. Since January 2019, CLO Virtual Fashion LLC (CLO US office) has officially been registering VAT MOSS (Sales Tax) in Ireland (EU). Since our online license sales are handled by our US office, all of our Individual license pricing will be in effect according to the regulation below. From January 2015, new legislation came into force that affects the sale of digital services to customers in other EU countries. Digital services include broadcasting, telecommunications, and electronic services (which includes software products). The VAT rate that is calculated for this type of transaction is based on the place supplying the service. The legislation that is regulating MOSS rules is: Council Directive (EU) 2017/2455 - Supplies of services and distance sales of goods (VAT e-commerce package). Council Directive 2008/8/EC - Place of supply of services. Council Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1042/2013 - Place of supply of services. This means if your billing address is under the EU region, VAT rates for each country will be added to your purchase. Austria 20% Belgium 21% Bulgaria 20% Czech Republic 21% Denmark 25% Germany 19% Estonia 20% Ireland 23% Greece 24% Spain 21% France 20% Croatia 25% Italy 22% Cyprus 19% Latvia 21% Lithuania 21% Luxembourg 17% Hungary 27% Malta 18% Netherlands 21% Poland 23% Portugal 23% Romania 19% Slovenia 22% Slovakia 20% Finland 24% Sweden 25% UK 20% If you would like to discover more regarding VAT MOSS, please review the file attached.

Title: Can I create Patterns from scratch in CLO?
Content: Yes, you can create patterns from scratch in CLO software. Please refer to the tutorial videos below: 1. Making a pattern -- You will learn how to make a basic pattern block from scratch. 2. Drafting a Pattern -- You will learn how to combine the CLO editing tools to draft a bodice pattern and a sleeve. 3. From Pattern to Production -- You will learn the whole garment creation process in CLO, making it ready for production. *Please refer to Create and Edit Pattern manuals in CLO Help Center. On the other hand, CONNECT offers over 700 free patterns for both female and male versions, allowing you to easily start customizing without the need to create a pattern. Please visit the CONNECT platform.

Title: Pin (Lasso)
Content: List of Contents Pin (Lasso) Create Pin Move Pin Delete Pin Invert Pin Selection Create Pins on a Segment Create Pins on a Pattern Pin (Lasso) - Create Pins on 3D Garments to fix parts of the Garment during Simulation and Animation. - Hold down the Pin (Box) tool on the 3D toolbar to access the child menus. Then, select the Pin (Lasso) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Pin (Lasso) Create Pin - Select the Pin (Lasso) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Patterns in the 2D window and 3D window will appear in red Mesh structure. - Click and drag on the Pattern to freehand desired shape of Lasso selection and apply Pins within the Lasso selection Move Pin - Activate the Simulation tool. Click and drag the Pin on the 3D Garment as the Garment moves along the mouse. - Deactivate the Simulation tool. Click the Pin to access the Gizmo tool. Use the Gizmo to move the selected Pin. Simulate again to apply the change to the 3D Garment. Delete Pin - To delete Pins on particular area, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to click and drag to encompass the desired area in the 2D window. Pins created on that area will be deleted. Invert Pin Selection - To invert the Pin selection, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to click and drag on the 3D Garment. - Pins will be created on the parts originally did not have Pins and will be highlighted in red. Create Pins on a Segment - Double click on the Pattern outline in the 2D or 3D window to create Pins on a segment. Create Pins on a Pattern - Double click within the Pattern in the 2D or 3D window to create Pins on a Pattern.

Title: What is CLO Verified?
Content: CLO OFFICIAL VERIFICATION CLO Verified is not a training, but an assessment of your skills in CLO Available for any CLO user with an Active Individual or Student License. No Enterprise Licenses can be used The test is broken into 3 different parts Build a garment from a DXF pattern. Correct a built garment that needs to be fixed/edited [similar to what you would be tasked with working in the industry]. Combine the 2 garments to create a full look which you will render in CLO. A Visual Quality Standards document will be sent the week before the test that will provide you with guidelines for the project submission. You will receive all tech packs, patterns, and necessary materials the day of the test for all 3 parts. Once completed, you will be notified 2-3 weeks after the test by email. You will receive both the outcome (Pass/Fail) and feedback about the files you have submitted. CERTIFICATE &amp BADGE All participants who pass the test will receive the CLO Verified Certificate, the only CLO recognized certificate, as well as the CLO Verified Badge which can be added to LinkedIn or other social media to show others their proven level of CLO expertise. PRACTICE ASSESSMENT We recommend all users take the self-graded Practice Test before signing up and paying for the Official Verification. This test is very similar but slightly shorter than the Official Verification and includes a Visual Quality Standards Guide to help you. Passing the CLO Verified Practice Test does not guarantee that you will pass the Official Verification, but it does mean that you should possess the skills needed to do so. Also, passing the practice test does not make you CLO Verified. To become CLO Verified you must take and Pass the Official Verification which the CLO Academic Team reviews and grades. **CURRENTLY THE CLO VERIFIED PRACTICE &amp OFFICIAL VERIFICATION ARE ONLY AVAILABLE IN ENGLISH** THINK YOURE READY? Do you use CLO regularly [15+ hours a week] with a focus on the CLO garment construction workflow? Are you able to quickly troubleshoot issues within CLO? Are you comfortable with Tech-Packs and Visual Quality Standards? To sign up for the Waitlist for alerts about upcoming tests and/or take the Practice Assessment please head over to the CLO Academy HERE

Title: Edit V-Ray Render Properties
Content: Objective Configure render properties for the final render image. Location Render Toolbar Render Properties. Operation Select the tool/menu in Location. Render properties appear in the Property Editor. Refer to the below table and edit the settings as needed. Option Description Render Engine Render Engine Choose the computer engine to run the render. CPU Run the render with CPU. GPU (CUDA) Run the render with GPU (CUDA). GPU (OpenCL) Run the render with GPU (OpenCL). This option does not appear in Mac. CPU Supporting Use CPU along with GPU when rendering. Toggle off this option to not use CPU. Note: This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as GPU (CUDA). Low GPU Priority Lower GPU priority when rendering. GPU is firstly used in other functions and then used in render. Note: This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as either GPU (CUDA) or GPU (OpenCL). Finish Conditions Noise Threshold Set the Noise Threshold for the final render image. The default value is 0.050 and the range is between 0.001 and 0.100. The higher the Noise Threshold is, the more the noise is in the final render image. Max, Render Time (min) The time used for rendering is about two minutes on average when default settings are used for render, light, and image/video properties. However, any modification on the properties may alter the render time. With this option, decide the maximum time that can be used for rendering per image. Quality Adjust the render quality of lights and materials. The Quality can be adjusted to four levels: Low, Medium, High, and Very High. As the option is set towards Very High, render speed decreases. Note: * Increase the Quality to render white fur. * Increase the Quality to express light reflections more realistically when textures are added to the studio environment such as the wall and floor. Light Adjust the quality of the light. Material Adjust the quality of materials. Mesh Optimization (Final Render Only) Knitwear Optimize the knitwear mesh in the invisible camera area of the final rendered image. This option only appears when Camera Lens is selected as Default. Frustum Culling No knitwear mesh is created outside the view frustum. A minor difference may appear in the final rendered image when Frustum Culling is enabled. This setting removes all meshes that are out of the camera's view. LOD Level of Detail. The number of knitwear meshes is reduced based on their distance from the camera, with greater distances resulting in fewer meshes. Color Mapping Calibrate the final image color. Type (ver 7.2) Choose the type of Color Mapping. Reinhard The closer the Burn value is to 1.0, the more the image color is multiplied simply by the brightness, and the closer it is to 0.0, the more the color is saturated by the brightness. HSV exponential Similar to Reinhard's Burn value of 0.0, the ratio of color (RGB) remains. Note: Use the Open, Save buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the setting. To optimize the render speed, please refer to the below directions. 1. When your OS is Windows: a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select GPU (CUDA) for Engine for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select GPU (OpenCL) for Engine for faster render time. 2. When your OS is Mac: a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select GPU (CUDA) for Engine for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select CPU for Engine for faster render time.

Title: Edit V-Ray Image/ Video Properties
Content: List of Contents Image/Video Properties Set Image/Video options Set Image Size Set Background Set Save Option Configure image/ video properties depending on the final output of the rendered 3D Garment. Image/Video Properties Click on the Image/ Video Properties tool in the Render toolbar. Set Image/Video options Option Description Image/ Video Select in which media the 3D Garment is to be extracted. Image Extract the rendered 3D Garment as a single image. Viewpoint Current View Render the 3D Garment with the current view. Custom View Select a view the 3D Garment is rendered from the Custom View. Colorways Render all colorways or select the colorways in the Colorway mode as desired by clicking the Select Colorway button. Turntable Images Extract the 3D Garment as a collection of rendered images, showing the 3D Garment in 360º. Image Count Set the number of images to be rendered. Higher the Image Count is, from more view points the 3D Garment is shot. Direction Counterclockwise Renders the 3D Garment counterclockwise. Clockwise Renders the 3D Garment clockwise. Save Video Save the rendered video as a video file. Total Duration Set duration for the whole video. Frame Duration Set duration for each frame. Animation Render and export recorded animation as images or a video by selecting the frame region. Region Entire Region Render the whole recording. Play Region Only render the Play Region designated by the user. Save Video Save the rendered animation as a video file. FPS Set the frame count for the video. Set Image Size Option Description Image Size Set the size for the final render image. Select among the provided options, or select Custom to input values arbitrarily. Orientation Portrait The image is laid out vertically. Landscape The image is laid out horizontally. Width Set the width of the image. Height Set the height of the image. Maintain Ratio Toggle the option On, to maintain the ratio between Height and Width of the image. Resolution (ppi) Adjust the image's resolution. Set Background Option Description Background Color Assign the background color. Texture Apply a background image to render. The image is automatically adjusted to the screen Transparency Make the background transparent. Note: You can also set a transparent background when saving the rendered 3D costume as a turntable (GIF) type.(ver 2024.0) Set Save Options Option Description Save File Name Name the saved file. Project Name Name the saved file with the Project file's name. Costume Name Name the saved file arbitrarily. File Path Designated the file saving path. Click on the Show in Saved Folder tool to open the designated saving path and view saved images. File Format Choose the format of the rendered image between JPG and PNG. Panoramic Custom Views Saves images rendered from multiple custom views as one image. If there are multiple colorways checking Panoramic Colorways option On will save a combined/Panoramic image of all the colorways along with separate images. Note: The View Point must be set to 'Current View,' and the colorway must be set to 'All' or 'Custom'. Video Codec Set the codec to use when recording video. Note: From ver 6.0, it is available to save MP4/AVI for Windows and MOV files for MAC without installing a separate codec. Note: Use the Open, Save buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the setting.

Title: Pin (Box)
Content: List of Contents Pin (Box) Create Pin Move Pin Delete Pin Invert Pin Selection Create Pins on a Segment Create Pins on a Pattern Pin (Box) - Create Pins on 3D Garments to fix parts of the Garment during Simulation and Animation. - Select the Pin (Box) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Pin (Box) Create Pin - Select the Pin (Box) tool from the 3d toolbar. - Patterns in the 2D window and 3D window will appear in red Mesh structure. - Click and drag on the Patterns to apply Pins within the marquee box. Move Pin - Activate the Simulation tool. Click and drag the Pin on the 3D Garment as the Garment moves along the mouse. - Deactivate the Simulation tool. Click the Pin to access the Gizmo tool. Use the Gizmo to move the selected Pin. Simulate again to apply the change to the 3D Garment. Delete - To delete Pins on particular area, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to click and drag to encompass the desired area. Pins created on that area will be deleted. Invert Pin Selection - To invert the Pin selection, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to click and drag on the 3D Garment. - Pins will be created on the parts originally did not have pins and will be highlighted in red. Create Pins on a Segment - Double click on the Pattern outline in the 2D or 3D window to create Pins on a segment. Create Pins on a Pattern - Double click within the Pattern in the 2D or 3D window to create Pins on a Pattern.

Content: Objective Zip or unzip zippers as needed. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Follow the location indicated above. Click &amp drag on the slider. Title: How to succeed with CLO Academy
Content: REGISTRATION &amp ENROLLMENT To sign up for CLO Academy, please visit this Registration Form. Please visit the CLO Academy Catalog Page for our available courses. When you have added the course to the cart and are going through checkout, be sure to keep your browser window open. Often this takes a few moments and if you close the window it will cause an issue between purchase and enrollment in the course. If you have any issues or questions, please email us at cloacademy@clo3d.com. COURSEWORK You will need to progress through the courses in sequence. Be sure to take your time, take notes, and pay close attention to the lessons You can take each Quiz twice if you like. The second attempt will be recorded as your grade. Go through the courses entirely, especially the INTRO TO CLO Courses. The instructors review the Quizzes and Submissions and adjust grading accordingly. *CLO has a no-refund policy. This applies to all subscriptions and one-time fees for CLO Academy Online. Please do not make any purchases with CLO Academy Online if you do not agree with our refund policy and the terms &amp conditions. Use of or access to CLO Academy Online in any way confirms your acceptance of our refund policy* FAQ There are a lot of courses/resources online, but its hard to figure out whats best for me. CLO Academy is a centralized, comprehensive learning experience that guides users through their CLO journey like a proper university program. Its taught in the way that we, at CLO, believe it should be learned - from years of experience training enterprise users, academics, and individuals. This is how you should learn CLO if you are interested in using it professionally. We want to ensure that those using CLO are using it correctly weve found that even users who consider themselves intermediate/experienced may not know how to do everything the best way. I looked at fashion school courses but they were too expensive. We tried to make CLO Academy as affordable as possible while providing the highest level of quality and support for our learners. I just want a place where I can learn everything, step by step, and ask questions if I get stuck. With CLO Academy, you can follow a guided curriculum that you know you can trust, without having to search through tons of unverified courses online. Our instructors and support team are also available to assist you with any questions or challenges you face. Im already an experienced user, how can I validate my credentials? CLO Verified was developed in response to frequent requests from our individual users. By successfully passing the CLO Individual User Verification, users receive a certification that can be added to their resume, LinkedIn, or portfolio, signaling to potential clients and employers that they possess a solid understanding of the software and are proficient in its use. Unlike courses on other platforms, these credentials are verified by CLO designers and include official CLO branding. Im not seeing any courses Im interested in. Listening to our community is key, and were committed to releasing more content designed for the ever-evolving needs of the industry. You can expect to see more courses on topics based on your feedback. Where do I ask questions, if I have them? Learners can message the instructor directly in the Journal or via messages with the course. We have a dedicated Discord channel for learners. (How can I join CLO Discord?) You can also reach us at cloacademy@clo3d.com for any CLO Academy related questions.

Title: Edit 3D Garment
Content: List of Contents Edit Style Line Scale/ Move Style Line Draw Style Line Objective Edit 3D garment easily by moving point and line by keeping its shape. Location 3D Toolbar Style Line Edit / Scale / Add Tool Operation Edit Style Line Click the tool/menu indicated. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. Pattern outline and point appear with a black outline. Click on the point drag and move. The line and the point sewn are moved together. Or click on the segment drag it. The curvature of the line is now adjustable. Scale/ Move Style Line Click the tool/menu indicated. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. Pattern outline and point appear translucent. Click on the segment drag it. The garment is scaled or moved with the sewn lines in the drag direction. Draw Style Line Click the tool/menu indicated. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. Pattern outline and point appear translucent. Hover on a Segment, a blue point will appear, click to start the new Style Line. A point is added to the selected point. Draw a curved line by clicking within the pattern piece, then double click on the segment where you want the new Style Line to end, or draw a straight line by double-clicking the endpoint. The pattern piece cut along the style line added. Note: - The function that allows you to scale or move one side of the sewn lines is excluded in the 6.2 version. The new feature with the improvement of usability will be provided. - While Editing/Scaling/Moving Style Line, right click to enter the desired dimension. (ver 7.1)

Content: Objective Draw lines on an avatar and extract patterns. Location Main Menu 3D Garment 3D Pen (Avatar) 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment 3D Pen (Avatar) 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Avatar) If there is a garment on the avatar, the garment appears translucent. Hover over the avatar. A black dot follows the mouse. Click on the desired position on the avatar to create line or shape. The line or shape appears on the avatar in black. Title: Render Output Improvement (Graininess, Noise)
Content: Where to Start Once your garment or look is finished, make sure you use the Hi-Res Garment tool and simulate to see the realistic drape. Next, go to the Render Menu Render to enter the Render Mode. Click to start an Interactive Render. As you view the preview, a good place to start is to use the default settings set up the image size as desired use a plain background (with an image vignette if desired) PNG file format is lossless and will therefore give you better quality than the JPEG reset the lighting to Default (Studio Low Contrast) &amp activate ground shadow (this effect is a must when rendering a full avatar) Windows users: use the GPU Engine Noise Threshold set at 0.05 Max Render Time = 20 min Light &amp Material Quality at Medium If you start here and create a final render, stop Interactive Render and click Final Render. Watch this complete and take note how long it takes. From here, you can make adjustments to the lighting and render properties to improve the image quality. Further Considerations Creating a beautiful image in CLO can be tricky at times. You need to balance the complexity of your project with the limitations of your hardware and the amount of time your computer will take to give you the final result. Here are a few things to consider How does your hardware match up to our system requirements? It is better to go towards the Recommended rather than Minimum. If your computer matches the minimum requirements, yes, it may work, but it will not be a good experience. You will quickly run into speed limitations not only while rendering, but with simulating as your garments get more complex. The amount of RAM in your computer will make the biggest difference with speed. What materials did you use? Are there any metals, sparkles, shiny areas on the fabrics, buttons, zippers, snaps, etc.? Anything that will reflect light while rendering can add more time to the rendering process. Have you added accessories or objects in the scene that have glass or metal? Did you create a mirror or place a ground plane that is very shiny? Think about your environment. It may be awesome to have a detailed room around your avatar and garment, but opting for a simple, plain background will not only reduce rendering time, but also focus the viewers attention on the garment. How complex is the garment or garments making up the looks? Is there visible internal layers or multiple layered garments? Are you using lots of buttons, zippers, graphics, prints, etc.? Is there puckering or have you activated Realistic Seamline while using the Fill tool? What image size are you using? It is recommended you pick from the pixel size options (640 x 480, etc.) as this will reduce the rendering time. The paper size layouts may seem attractive but the document/pixel ratios can cause a slowing of the rendering process. If needed, changing the resolution (ppi) will slow down the rendering process. Check your Render Properties: Are you rendering fur? It is recommended to switch to CPU Engine to get better results, but it will take longer. So you need to decide whether the slower rendering is beneficial. What is your Noise Threshold? Default 0.05, the lower you go, the better the details but it will take longer. Max Render Time Based on all the variables, CLO will do the best it can with the time you have allotted. Light and Material Quality will also affect the length of your render. Note: If you want to render an animation (rather than capturing the 3D window), always do a single render to start. The time it took to render that one image should be multiplied by the number of frames in the animation. Example: image rendering time = 5 minutes frames in animation = 450 how long the render animation will take: 2250 minutes or 37.5 hours (a day and a half)

Title: Select Mesh (Box)
Content: List of Contents Select Mesh (Box) Select Multiple Areas Delete Selection Invert Selection Select a Segment Select a Pattern Select Mesh (Box) - Select and move 3D Garment Mesh as needed. - Select the Select Mesh (Box) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Select Mesh (Box) Select Multiple Areas - Select the Select Mesh (Box) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Patterns in the 2D window and 3D window will appear in yellow-green Mesh structure. - Click and drag on the Pattern to create marquee box to select desired area. - Hold down the Shift and Ctrl keys on the keyboard to select multiple areas on the 3D Garment. Delete - To deselect particular areas, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click and drag to encompass the desired area in the 2D window. The encompassed area will be deselected. Invert Selection - To invert the selection, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to click and drag on the 3D Garment. - The areas originally not selected will be selected and vice-versa. - The selected area will be highlighted in yellow-green. Select a Segment - Double click on the Pattern outline in the 2D or 3D window to select a segment. Select a Pattern - Double click within the Pattern in the 2D or 3D window to select a Pattern.

Title: Zipper
Content: List of Contents Zipper Creating Zipper Unzip/Zip Zipper Edit Zipper Tape/ Slider Property Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Zipper - Create and express zippers easily and quickly. - Select the Zipper tool from the 3D toolbar. Creating Zipper - Select the Zipper tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. - The Pattern outlines and Internal Lines on the 3D Garment will appear as dashed lines. - Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the Zipper will be placed. - Click once and drag the mouse cursor along the Pattern outline or Internal Line. - Double click to complete the first half of the Zipper. - Hover the mouse over the Pattern outlines or Internal Lines where the other half of the Zipper will be placed. - Repeat the same procedure. A blue dot will appear to guide the length of the first half of the Zipper. - When the Zipper is established, the Zipper tape and the Zipper slider will appear along the designated Pattern outlines or Internal Lines. - The Zipper slider will always be located at the starting position where Zipper was placed - Select the Simulation from the 3D Toolbar. - The Zipper will fasten. Unzip/ Zip Zipper - With Simulation off, select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar to partially unzip or Zip the Zipper. - Click on the Zipper slider, and it will be highlighted in yellow. - Click and drag the Zipper slider along the Zipper tape. A grey slider will follow along the mouse to preview the location. - Release the mouse to finalize Zipper sliders location. - Select the Simulation from the 3D toolbar. - Only the designated part of the Zipper will fasten or unfasten. Editing Zipper Tape/ Slider Property - Use the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar to select either the Zipper tape or the Zipper slider. Zipper Tape Width (MM) - Type in a specific value to assign width to the Zipper tape. Thickness (MM) - Type in a specific value to assign thickness to the Zipper tape. - Change the Garment Rendering Style to Thick Textured Surface to see Zipper tapes thickness. Fasten Zipper - Toggle on/off the option to completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. - Toggle Off the Fasten Zipper option to unzip the zipper. Material - Texture - Change the texture of the Zipper tape. - Add Normal Map and check on/off Desaturation to convert the texture into greyscale. Material - Color - Change the color of the Zipper tape. - Adjust Ambient Intensity and Diffuse Intensity as needed. Ambient Intensity expresses the effect of ambient light. Diffuse Intensity controls the intensity of the applied texture image and color. - Adjust Specular Color as needed. With the Shininess option, modify the sheen of the Zipper tape. - Add Specular Map to assign how Specular Color is applied to the Zipper slider. - Adjust Emission Color to set the color that emits from the Zipper tape. Fold - Strength: set the strength of the fold of the Sewing Line between the Pattern and the Zipper. - Angle: set the fold angle between the Zipper and the Pattern to express the fold . Particle Distance(mm) - Adjust Particle Distance for Zipper Tapes(ver4.1.0). Zipper Slider Shape - Choose the design of the Zipper slider. Size - Select the size of the Zipper slider from the provided presets, or type in a desired percentage to adjust manually. Fasten Zipper - Completely Zip or unzip the Zipper. - Toggle On/Off the Reverse Zipper Direction option to locate the Zipper pull at either end of the Zipper. - Toggle On/Off the Move to Opposite Side option to attach the Zipper pull to either half of the Zipper tape when the Zipper is unzipped. Material - Adjust provided options to add texture or colors to the Zipper slider. - Adjust the Opacity to express the Zipper slider as translucent or solid. Zipper Tape/ Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu - Select the Select/Move tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to 2D window. - Right click on the Zipper tape/ slider to be edited. - The pop-up menu with options below will appear. Zipper Tape Delete - Delete the Zipper tape and slider. - Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select Delete. - Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. Reverse (Right Clicked) - Similar to the Free Sewing tool, both halves of the Zipper tape need to be established in the same direction. If they are sewn incorrectly, the Zipper tape may twist. - If Zipper appears to be deformed during Simulation, right-click and select Reverse to reverse the Sewing Line. Flip Normal (Right Clicked Teeth) - Flip the fabric side of the Zipper tape in the 3D window. - Select the Zipper Sewing Line, right-click and select Flip Normal. Deactivate/Freeze - Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper tape to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. - Right-click on Zipper seam line, select Deactivate or Freeze. - To Reactivate or Unfreeze the deactivated/frozen Zipper tape, right-click the Zipper seam line again and select Reactivate or Unfreeze. Zipper Slider Delete -Delete the Zipper Tape and Slider. - Select the Zipper seam line, right-click and select Delete. - Or, Select the Zipper seam line, and hit the Delete Key on the Keyboard. Deactivate/Freeze - Deactivate or Freeze the selected Zipper Pull to fix and exclude the selected Zipper from Simulation. - Right-click on Zipper Slider, select Deactivate or Freeze.

Title: Non-testable Fabrics for CLO Fabric Digitization Service
Content: Fabric Type Physical Properties Testing 3D Image Scanning Comments Short Fur O X Short Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Long Fur X X Long Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Feather Yarns X X The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Foil O X Foil can be expressed by setting the Iridescene option for the material type of CLO Fabric. PVC O X PVC can be expressed by setting the Iridescene option for the material type of CLO Fabric. Glitter O X Glitter can expressed by setting the Glitter option for the material type of CLO fabric. Sequin X X Sequin can be expressed using CLO. Pleats X X Pleated fabric can be created by using CLO. Elastic Band X X The unavailability of a suitable swatch size makes it difficult to measure physical properties. Wide Stripe Fabric (Made of different yarns) X X The combination of the multiple properties makes it difficult to measure physical properties accurately in a single fabric. Dangling Embellishments X X The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Complicated Novelty Yarns X X The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Multi-layer Fabric X X If the multiple fabric layers are only partially attached, it can affect the accuracy of physical property measurements. Crinkled Fabric X X Fabric with processed crinkles is difficult to measure its stretch accurately. Openwork Lace X X Fabric with a very loose weave is difficult to measure its stretch and bending properties.

Title: Register API Plug-In
Content: Objective By using CLO API, develop and add customized features to CLO. For example, develop a feature to collect necessary BOM information from a 3D garment produced in CLO. Then, add and use the customized feature in CLO. Location Main Menu Settings User Settings CLO API Operation Follow the path indicated below: Main Menu Settings User Settings CLO API Click the Add button on the right top corner. A File Explorer dialog appears where you can search *.dll or *.dylib files. Select and Open the desired *.dll or *.dylib file. The Register Plug-In window appears. Refer to below and configure an UI for the plug-in to be added. Option Description Name Name the plug-in. Position Main Menu, child menus for the selected Main Menu, and any additional corresponding child menus appear in order. Select a desired menu and choose the plug-in's position in terms of the selected menu. Click OK to complete the registration. Note: Registered plug-ins also appear in below path: Main Menu Settings Plug-in Please Contact Us, if you have any questions.
